text:
jordan: Draft PRD for 'Launch gating: audit & key mgmt' posted. Need quick alignment on SOC2/ISO acceptance criteria + KMS/HSM scope. Quick asks: what retention defaults, what keys do we require for hosted vs private, and minimal audit events we must keep. PTAL.

sophia: Can you paste the acceptance checklist here? Are we blocking GA on any of these or just documenting?

jordan: Short checklist:
```
- Audit logs: immutable, tamper-evident, queryable
- Default retention: 365d (hosted), customer-configurable up to 7y
- KMS: Redwood-managed for hosted, customer-managed (KMS/HSM) for Private
- Audit export: S3-compatible, signed manifests + incremental export API
- Evidence: per-route token-level cost traces + error sampling
```
Blocking for GA: tamper-evidence + export endpoint.

liam: SOC2 baseline: immutable logs, access controls, integrity checks (HMAC), and retention policy documented. For ISO we should also show key custody model and separation of duties. HSM requirement only for customers with regulated workloads; don't default all hosted keys to HSM (cost). Also: include log integrity proofs (periodic snapshots).

maya: Implementation concerns:
- storing full request payloads will spike storage -> suggest event schema: metadata + hashed identifiers, optional full payload for Dedicated/Private
- need sampling or TTL for debug-level fields and embeddings to control costs
- KV cache traces and prefix cache logs can blow up quickly, add aggregation and rollup jobs
I'll sketch perf/cost numbers in the PRD.

ravi: Legal: watch out for PII and cross-border transfer when exports are enabled. For EU customers we need DSAR support + ability to redact or pseudonymize logs. Retention >2y may need additional business justification. Record these as compliance gating questions.

ops-bot: [automated] Ticket created: INF-4521 'Audit logs export API + retention config' -> assignee @maya, due 2026-03-27.

sophia: Product tradeoffs to call out: cost vs completeness, default safe settings for hosted, opt-in extended retention for enterprise, rollout plan (canary with Dedicated customers then Private). Also list edge cases: high-throughput embedding pipelines, customer-requested deletion, and legal holds.

jordan: OK — action items: liam to write SOC2/ISO acceptance block (EOW), maya to scope perf impact and draft export API (mid next week), ravi to confirm legal thresholds for retention and PII handling. I'll update the PRD with these items and set a quick review meeting. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
